content:
ada: Quick report from the overnight perf sweep: after the adaptive-kselector v3 rollout, small-multi-frame requests are showing p95 tail regressions on host-side parse+streaming. p95 went from ~74ms -> ~130ms on our http2 multiplex workload.
kai: Interesting. Did you run flamegraphs or traces?
rebekah: I grabbed a perf top and some tcpdump samples. Top stacks:
```
25% host-proxy _stream_frame_emit
15% host-proxy kv_lookup_miss
12% libc writev (lots of tiny writes)
6% kernel select_variant_v3
```
yusuf: So kernel selector is now preferring tiny-kernel for sub-4-token requests. That kernel sets adaptive_batch_size=1 and disables the previous frame coalescer. It was aimed at single-request latency but seems to punish multiplexed small-reqs.
ada: Also saw an increase in syscall rates (writev) and more frequent KV cache mutex contention windows around handshake. Likely the earlier tokenizer prefetch change (preparse-eager) causes more early chunk emits which prevents batching.
kai: Could we toggle coalescing only on http2 multiplexer path? Maybe tiny-kernel + http2 should keep coalesce=true.
rebekah: Quick A/B I ran on staging: keep kselector v3, but flip http2.coalesce_frames=true -> p95 drops to 82ms; KV hit rate recovered by ~4pp. Command used: `./tools/bench --mux http2 --small-reqs --qps 300 --duration 60s`
ada: Nice. Another idea: set TCP_CORK / SO_SNDBUF bump in proxy for the write path so multiple small writev calls are combined by kernel. This avoids adding artificial delay.
yusuf: Risky on latency-critical flows, but for multiplexed streams it looks safe if we scope it to M=small-frame batches.
ci-bot: canary deploy scheduled: canary/adaptive-kselector-v3 -> staging at 3598765900 by rebekah (note: http2.coalesce_frames=true for canary).
kai: If canary results match staging A/B, we'll ship a targeted heuristic: keep tiny-kernel routing, but override coalesce for http2 mux and set kernel hint `batch_delay_ms=1` as a safety net.
rebekah: Action items: (1) rebekah to post perf snapshots from canary (2) ada to correlate tokenizer chunk timestamps with KV miss spikes (3) yusuf to prototype TCP_CORK scoped change and run quick bench.
ada: I'll add a small test to the perf suite that runs multiplexed 2-token workloads nightly to catch regressions.
yusuf: I'll open PR for coalesce-scope change if canary is green.
ada: thanks all. Marking this as perf-regression/low-priority but scheduled for fix-next-week if canary reproduces. :thumbsup:
